result.target_summary: The NVIDIA Data Center platform accelerates compute-intensive workloads like AI and HPC, offering better performance and power efficiency than CPU-only approaches, and is deployed in cloud, on-premises, and edge environments via systems, subsystems, modules, software, and services.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures focus on the Data Center platform's role in accelerating compute-intensive workloads and emphasize its superior performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD describe their Data Center segment as a portfolio of hardware products (CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators) designed to accelerate specific workloads. NVIDIA emphasizes its platform accelerates 'compute-intensive workloads, such as AI, data analytics... delivering significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.' AMD similarly states it leverages its technology to 'address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market' and that different combinations of its products 'enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.' Both disclosures highlight the focus on AI and the competitive advantage of accelerated computing over traditional CPUs.

sentences.text: The NVIDIA Data Center platform is focused on accelerating the most compute-intensive workloads, such as AI, data analytics, graphics and scientific computing, delivering significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.
We leverage our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA identifies its deployment environment as 'cloud, hyperscale, on-premises and edge data centers,' focusing on the platform's reach. AMD provides a more detailed view of its 'Hyperscale Customer Base,' noting that 'large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers' purchase a substantial portion of its products. AMD explicitly links these hyperscale customers to 'AI workloads such as generative AI models,' mirroring NVIDIA's focus on AI acceleration, while NVIDIA's disclosure is broader regarding deployment venues (including edge and on-premises) without specifying the customer type as heavily.

sentences.text: It is deployed in cloud, hyperscale, on-premises and edge data centers.

Large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers directly and indirectly purchase a substantial portion of our data center-focused products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SOCs.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.
